newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to unveil plan to boost training, jobs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to unveil plan to boost training, jobs.

text.p: Brazil will unveil on Wednesday a plan to beef up professional training, teach millions of workers to read and write and help small enterprises create more jobs, officials said.

Two agreements to be signed by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, business groups and state-owned banks include the release of 590 million reais for several ongoing programs to provide training and credit for small companies and farms.

In a radio address Tuesday, Cardoso said Brazil needed to double the educational standards of Brazilian workers -- who on average only make it through four years of schooling -- to better compete in a global economy.
Brazil's Constitution states that every citizen has the right to eight years of education. But an estimated 24 million Brazilians over the age of 10 are illiterate.
"Tomorrow we will take a big step towards improving the educational standards of our workers," Cardoso said in the address.

As well as reducing illiteracy, the plan seeks to provide on-the-job training for five million workers each year via a network of 30,000 public schools, universities, trade unions, and private educational foundations.
